summary: Review the implemented spell-system across correctness, security, UX-fidelity, integration; verify each finding

blockers: UI cast flow is completely broken (two compounding blockers on the same primary path): (1) MaestroClient.activateSpell hardcodes `invokerSessionId: null` (MaestroClient.ts:793) but the server's spellActivationSchema (validation.ts:561) is `safeId.optional()` inside a `.strict()` object, which rejects null — every UI cast/activation 400s with VALIDATION_ERROR before reaching the handler. Fix: change schema to `safeId.nullable().optional()`. CLI works only because it omits the field.

UI cast flow runtime crash: MaestroClient.activateSpell declares return `{ activeSpells, sessionIds }` (MaestroClient.ts:790) but the server actually returns `{ spell, sessions }` (SpellService.ts:885-927, passed verbatim by spellRoutes.ts:199-200). The unchecked `response.json()` cast hides this from tsc, so all three packages typecheck clean, but useSpellActivationStore.castSpell reads `result.sessionIds.length` (line 52) which is undefined at runtime → TypeError, caught and surfaced as 'Cast failed'. The toast/5s-undo success path never completes. Fix: align client type to `{ spell, sessions }` and derive `sessionIds = result.sessions.map(s => s.sessionId)`. deactivateSpell works because the server genuinely returns `sessionIds` there.
prioritizedFixes: [HIGH] Task.spellIds is never resolved into manifest.spells — the entire P5 task-attach auto-activate chain is dead at the producer. Consumer (worker-init.ts:186, orchestrator-init.ts:176, spell-auto-activator.ts) and manifest schema are fully wired, but nothing populates manifest.spells: manifest-generator.ts is untouched by the diff and sessionRoutes.ts generateManifestViaCLI passes only --task-ids/--skills (no --spells). Net: assigning spells to a task has zero effect at spawn. Cleanest fix is server-side in sessionRoutes.ts after CLI manifest generation (server already has Task.spellIds + the Spell repo): collect unique spellIds from spawn tasks, resolve to ManifestSpell[], set manifest.spells, re-serialize. (This is the manifest-population gap, distinct from the verify-only Task.spellIds Zod item.)

[HIGH] Ensemble visual identity does not render at all (three related gaps). (a) Ensemble outermost ring never uses the ensemble color: RingSpec.ensembleColorId is never populated at any of the 3 ring hosts (SessionListItem/SpacesRail/AppWorkspace), so spellRingAttrs' `ensembleColorId ?? colorId` always falls back to the spell's own color — ensemble membership is visually indistinguishable from a solo spell. Fix: resolve via useEnsembleStore.ensembleById(id).color → resolveSpellColorId in a shared selector and pass ensembleColorId per ringSpec. (b) EnsembleGroup/EnsembleDock are fully implemented but have ZERO consumers — never mounted; session list/SpacesRail group only by team, so ensembles have no visible grouping container. Wire EnsembleGroup into the grouping path. (c) .pn-ensemble dashed-frame CSS (01 §3.5) and ensemble-breathe keyframe (§4.5) do not exist in any stylesheet; EnsembleGroup emits className=pn-ensemble but no rule matches. Note (c) is latent since ensemble UI is currently unmounted, but (a)/(b)/(c) together mean the ensemble feature surface is effectively non-functional.

[HIGH] Zero automated tests added for the entire spell system across all three packages. The core value — HookDispatcherService.composeResult exit-code/composition contract (gate-wins exit 2, continue-loop exit 2 on Stop, stdout concat, per-spell failMode open/closed) and CLI hook.ts applyResult translation — has no coverage, nor activation idempotency, invoke fan-out, or ensemble fan-out. Add focused unit tests (hook-dispatcher.test.ts, hook.test.ts). Separately, `bun run test` is already red from 5 pre-existing server suite failures (SessionRouteDependencies missing teamService/ptyHostService) that exist at base 3733ca6 and are NOT spell regressions — fix separately, do not block on them, but they mean there is no green safety net.

[MEDIUM] continue-loop seeded on UserPromptSubmit (spell_plan_first, FileSystemSpellRepository.ts:60-74) makes exit 2 BLOCK the user's first prompt instead of continuing. exit 2 only means 'continue' on the Stop hook; on UserPromptSubmit it blocks and surfaces the loop-continuation text as an error. Fix: bind spell_plan_first trigger to Stop (matching spell_self_critic precedent and the frozen taxonomy), and optionally gate composeResult's exit-2 branch to event==='Stop' as defense-in-depth.

[MEDIUM] Hook dispatch trusts body sessionId with no caller-ownership check (cross-session control). POST /api/hooks/dispatch reads sessionId from the body and acts on that session's activeSpells (continue-loop iteration bump, PTY prompt injection, notify side effects) with no verification the caller owns the session. The CLI sends X-Session-Id (hook.ts:74) but the server ignores it. Inconsistent with sibling gates (spawn requires coordinator role, mode_self_only). Fix: require X-Session-Id === body.sessionId (mirror the mode_self_only gate). Capped severity by the localhost single-token trust model, but inter-session isolation is clearly intended.

[MEDIUM] User-controlled spell matcher compiled to RegExp on the hot hook path (ReDoS / event-loop stall). matcherMatches() runs `new RegExp(matcher).test(target)` synchronously on every PreToolUse/PostToolUse dispatch against attacker-influenceable targets; matcher is validated only as z.string().max(500). A catastrophic-backtracking pattern stalls the single-threaded event loop, freezing all sessions. Fix: reject unsafe patterns at create/update via safe-regex refinement, and cap target length / use RE2 on the runtime path for legacy data.

[MEDIUM] 'Pause' on an active spell silently deactivates it and resets iteration/cast-order state on resume. The live Pause/Resume menu (ActiveSpellChip) maps to deactivate/re-activate, so Pause removes the ring entirely and Resume resets iteration to 0 and re-orders concentric rings (castAt=now). The designed `enabled` flag + HookDispatcher `!a.enabled` gate are unused; no endpoint flips enabled without removal. Minimal fix: remove the mislabeled Pause/Resume item (chip already only truly supports Deactivate). Preferred: add a real enabled-toggle endpoint that preserves state.

[MEDIUM] inject-prompt action double-delivers on stdout-surfacing hooks. execInjectPrompt both emits session:prompt_send (PTY) AND returns stdout, which the CLI applyResult writes unconditionally for every action (the server's comment claiming the CLI discriminates is false). On UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart a custom inject-prompt spell lands twice — the double-inject bug class P1 was meant to kill. Latent (no seed spell triggers it). Fix: drop the stdout field from execInjectPrompt's return.

[MEDIUM] Ring cast-pulse (--just-cast) entirely unwired — no @keyframes spell-cast-pulse, no .spell-ring--just-cast selector, no JS class toggle on any host (spec 01 §4.1). Distinctive cast feedback missing on all three boxes (rings still fade via base box-shadow). Add the keyframe/selector + a reduced-motion-gated transient class driven by spell:activated.

[MEDIUM] Iteration-tick motion fully absent — no @keyframes spell-iter-tick, the reduced-motion block references .spell-ring__tick/--ticking selectors that are never defined (dead CSS shipped), no useReducedMotion gate, and no spell:iteration_advanced WS event; iteration is hardcoded to 0 server-side and never incremented. Loop-spell forward-progress signal is inoperative. Fix CSS for self-consistency now; full fix needs a server iteration-advanced event.

[MEDIUM] Ringed host elements lack the mandated aria-label (spec 01 §5, locked WCAG-AA contract) announcing active spells, e.g. 'Session foo — 2 spells: Guardian, Test Sentinel'. None of the 3 hosts provide one (SpacesRail uses only title=session.name). data-spell-ring-names is set but not surfaced to AT; screen-reader users get no signal spells are active. Add a shared spellRingAriaLabel helper. (+N overflow buttons already have correct labels.)

[MEDIUM] Spell-detail color swatch uses raw server slug instead of resolved palette id (SpellDetailFlyout.tsx:116). Class is `sp-detail__swatch--${spell.color}` but CSS only defines the 10 UI palette ids; 8 of 9 seed slugs (rose/violet/sky/emerald/fuchsia/lime/cyan/indigo) match no rule and render uncolored. Fix: resolveSpellColorId(spell.color) before composing the class (same helper SpellCard uses); also fix data-spell-color on line 74.

[LOW] Seed (isDefault) spells can be mutated via PUT, silently weakening gate/fail-closed library spells. DELETE is guarded but UPDATE only preserves id/createdAt/isDefault, letting a caller flip a failMode:'closed' gate to failMode:'open' or action:'inject-prompt', persisted and merged over the seed while still showing isDefault in the UI. Latent today (failMode not yet enforced). Fix: restrict seed-spell updates to cosmetic fields, mirroring the delete guard.

[LOW] spell:activated WS payload omits the spell name, so ring tooltips/selectors show raw IDs ('spell_guardian' instead of 'Guardian'), breaking the data-spell-ring-names contract (UI_SPEC §7) and e2e selectors. One-line fix: add `spellName: spell.name` to the emit; the UI fallback already reads message.data.spellName.

[LOW] Picker library-row hover-tint contract (data-spell-color-id + --spell-row-hover-bg, spec 01 §1.5) not implemented; SpellCard uses local inline vars instead, and the keyboard-focused (aria-activedescendant) row has no visual treatment (data-focused has no matching CSS, aria-activedescendant never set). Fix: tag rows with data-spell-color-id, add the color-mix hover/selected/focused rule exposing --spell-row-hover-bg, and set aria-activedescendant.

[LOW] run-command seed spells (Test Sentinel, Lint-on-Edit) are silent no-ops — execRunCommand reads (spell as any).command which never exists on the Spell entity, so the branch returns empty stdout. 2 of 9 curated spells are inert when activated (documented v1 deferral pending CLI HookExecutor). Surface this (badge/disable the spells or return a deferral reason) so it isn't mistaken for working behavior.
summary.summary: NOT ship-ready. Two compounding blockers break the primary UI spell-cast path end-to-end: the client always sends invokerSessionId:null which the strict server Zod schema rejects (every cast 400s), and even past that the client's activateSpell return type fabricates a {activeSpells, sessionIds} shape the server never produces ({spell, sessions}), causing a runtime TypeError that surfaces as 'Cast failed'. Both typecheck clean only because of an unchecked response.json() cast, so the green build is misleading. Beyond casting, three HIGH gaps mean major advertised surfaces don't work: Task.spellIds never reaches manifest.spells (task auto-activation is a dead end at the producer), the entire ensemble visual identity is unrendered (ring color not threaded, EnsembleGroup/Dock never mounted, .pn-ensemble CSS absent), and the diff adds zero tests for the core exit-code/composition contract while `bun run test` is already red from pre-existing (non-spell) failures. A cluster of MEDIUM issues follows: a seeded continue-loop on UserPromptSubmit that blocks the user's first prompt, an unauthenticated cross-session hook-dispatch surface, a ReDoS-able user regex on the hot hook path, a mislabeled Pause that destroys loop state, inject-prompt double-delivery, three missing/dead motion-and-a11y contracts (cast pulse, iteration tick, host aria-label), and a colorless detail swatch. LOW items: mutable seed spells, raw-ID ring tooltips, missing picker hover-tint, and 2 inert run-command seed spells. The server dispatcher/composition logic itself appears sound; the failures are concentrated at the UI client contract, the spawn producer, and missing test/CSS/a11y wiring. Recommend fixing the two blockers and the three HIGH gaps (plus the UserPromptSubmit binding and the hook-dispatch ownership check) before shipping.

confirmed.title: UI activateSpell sends invokerSessionId: null, which the strict Zod schema rejects — every UI cast/activation 400s
confirmed.detail: MaestroClient.activateSpell() always sends `{ targetSessionIds, invokerSessionId: invokerSessionId ?? null }` (line 793). The server schema spellActivationSchema (validation.ts ~line 511) declares `invokerSessionId: safeId.optional()` inside a `.strict()` object, i.e. type `string | undefined` — it does NOT accept `null`. So when the UI casts a spell (the common case, no invoker), it posts `invokerSessionId: null`, Zod rejects it, and the route returns 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. This breaks the primary live-cast path from the UI entirely (the activation lifecycle). The CLI auto-activator (spell-auto-activator.ts) avoids this by omitting the field, so server/CLI work; only the UI is broken. Fix: either make the schema `safeId.nullable().optional()` (matches the activate route which already does `invokerSessionId ?? null`), or have the client omit the key when null. Note the deactivate/activate routes' own handlers already coerce `invokerSessionId ?? null`, confirming null was intended to be accepted.

verdict.title: UI activateSpell sends invokerSessionId: null, which the strict Zod schema rejects — every UI cast/activation 400s
verdict.reasoning:
Verified end-to-end against the diff and proven empirically with Zod.

1. UI client always sends explicit null: maestro-ui/src/utils/MaestroClient.ts line 793 — `body: JSON.stringify({ targetSessionIds, invokerSessionId: invokerSessionId ?? null })`. On the common cast path there is no invoker, so `null` is serialized into the JSON body. Confirmed at every UI caller: useSpellActivationStore.castSpell passes `input.invokerSessionId ?? null` (line 45) and setSpellEnabled calls `activateSpell(spellId, [sessionId])` with the arg undefined (line 77), which the client coerces to null.

2. Server schema rejects null: maestro-server/src/api/validation.ts lines 559-562 — `spellActivationSchema = z.object({ targetSessionIds: z.array(safeId).min(1), invokerSessionId: safeId.optional() }).strict()`. `safeId` is `z.string().regex(...)`. `.optional()` accepts string|undefined but NOT null. I ran the actual schema in maestro-server's node_modules: explicit null -> FAIL ('Invalid input: expected string, received null'); omitted -> PASS; string -> PASS.

3. The route returns 400 on this: spellRoutes.ts line 196 wires `validateBody(spellActivationSchema)`; validateBody (validation.ts line 623) returns `res.status(400).json({ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' })` on safeParse failure. So every UI cast 400s before reaching the handler.

4. Asymmetry confirmed: the CLI auto-activator (maestro-cli/src/services/spell-auto-activator.ts lines 21-23) posts to the same strict /activate route but OMITS invokerSessionId, so CLI works. The single-session CLI command (spell.ts line 182) likewise conditionally spreads `...(invokerSessionId ? { invokerSessionId } : {})`, omitting when falsy. Only the UI hardcodes null.

5. Intent confirmed: the activate handler (spellRoutes.ts line 199) already does `invokerSessionId ?? null` before calling the service, showing null was the intended in-handler representation; the schema simply never permitted null on the wire.

Not in the known-deferred list. This breaks the primary live-cast path from the UI entirely.
verdict.fix:
Make the schema accept null, matching the route handler's existing `invokerSessionId ?? null` coercion. In maestro-server/src/api/validation.ts (spellActivationSchema, line 561) change:

  invokerSessionId: safeId.optional(),
to
  invokerSessionId: safeId.nullable().optional(),

This is the minimal one-line fix and aligns the wire contract with how the handler already treats the field. (Alternatively, the UI client at MaestroClient.ts line 793 could omit the key when null, e.g. `body: JSON.stringify({ targetSessionIds, ...(invokerSessionId ? { invokerSessionId } : {}) })`, but the schema fix is preferable since it also covers any other caller and matches the handler's intent.) Note: the single-session invokeSpellSchema (validation.ts line 480) has the same `safeId.optional()` for invokerSessionId; it is currently safe only because CLI callers omit the field, so applying `.nullable()` there too would harden it against the same class of bug.

confirmed.title: activateSpell client return type is wrong; castSpell reads result.sessionIds which is undefined at runtime
confirmed.detail: MaestroClient.activateSpell declares it returns `{ activeSpells: ActiveSpell[]; sessionIds: string[] }` (line 790), but SpellService.activateSpell returns `{ spell: Spell; sessions: { sessionId; activeSpell }[] }` (SpellService.ts:885-928) — there is no `sessionIds` or `activeSpells` field. useSpellActivationStore.castSpell then does `const count = result.sessionIds.length` (useSpellActivationStore.ts:52) and builds the undo receipt from `result.sessionIds` (line 56). At runtime result.sessionIds is undefined, so `.length` throws a TypeError and the cast flow blows up after the POST. Schema-lockstep break between the route response and the client contract. Fix: align the client/return shape with the server (`{ spell, sessions }`) and derive sessionIds from `sessions.map(s => s.sessionId)`, or change the server to also return `sessionIds`.

verdict.title: activateSpell client return type mismatch crashes castSpell at runtime (result.sessionIds is undefined)
verdict.reasoning:
Verified end-to-end against the diff at 3733ca6...345435e (the spell-system branch feat/spell-system-server-dispatch; HEAD 345435e exists as the brief states).

Server side: SpellService.activateSpell (maestro-server/src/application/services/SpellService.ts:885-928) is typed and actually returns `{ spell: Spell; sessions: { sessionId: string; activeSpell: ActiveSpell }[] }`. It returns `{ spell, sessions }` at the end — there is NO `sessionIds` field and NO `activeSpells` field.

Route boundary: spellRoutes.ts:199-200 does `const result = await spellService.activateSpell(...); res.json(result);` — it passes the service return verbatim with zero remapping. So the HTTP response body is literally `{ spell, sessions }`.

Client side: MaestroClient.activateSpell (maestro-ui/src/utils/MaestroClient.ts:790) declares `Promise<{ activeSpells: ActiveSpell[]; sessionIds: string[] }>` and its body is just `return this.fetch(...)`. The private fetch<T> helper (line 76, 103) does `return await response.json()` — an unchecked cast to T. So the declared type is a lie the typechecker trusts; at runtime the object is `{ spell, sessions }`.

Consumer: useSpellActivationStore.castSpell (maestro-ui/src/stores/useSpellActivationStore.ts:42-64) calls activateSpell then does `const count = result.sessionIds.length` (line 52), builds the undo action from `result.sessionIds` (line 56), and returns `sessionIds: result.sessionIds` (line 64). At runtime `result.sessionIds` is undefined, so `undefined.length` throws a TypeError and the cast flow blows up immediately after the POST succeeds.

This explains why all three packages typecheck clean (the wrong declared return type plus the unchecked json() cast hides the mismatch from tsc) yet the primary cast path crashes at runtime. This is a genuine schema-lockstep break between the route response and the client contract on the main user-facing flow, not a deferred stub. Severity is a real functional blocker for casting.

confirmed.title: Task.spellIds is never resolved into manifest.spells — the entire P5 task-attach auto-activate chain is dead at the producer
confirmed.detail: The consumer side is fully wired: worker-init.ts and orchestrator-init.ts call autoActivateManifestSpells(manifest, sessionId), which POSTs /api/spells/:id/activate for each manifest.spells entry (spell-auto-activator.ts). The manifest schema (manifest-schema.ts) and ManifestSpell type (types/manifest.ts) both accept `spells`. BUT nothing ever populates manifest.spells: manifest-generator.ts has zero references to `spell`/`spellIds` (grep confirms), and the server never injects spells either (no `.spells`/`spellIds` usage in maestro-server/src/api or /application outside SpellService/Ensemble/HookDispatcher). Task.spellIds is persisted (TaskService.createTask spreads `...input`, and validation.ts accepts it), but the spawn pipeline never reads Task.spellIds, looks the spells up, and writes them into the generated manifest. Net effect: assigning spells to a task has no effect at spawn — task-attached spells never auto-activate. This is the core P5 'baked into manifest at spawn, auto-activate' decision left unimplemented on the producer end. (The brief lists only 'Task.spellIds Zod acceptance' as verify-only; the manifest population is a real gap, not the deferred item.)

verdict.title: Task.spellIds is never resolved into manifest.spells — P5 task-attach auto-activate is dead at the producer
verdict.reasoning:
VERIFIED from the diff and source.

CONSUMER SIDE IS FULLY WIRED:
- maestro-cli/src/commands/worker-init.ts:186 and orchestrator-init.ts:176 both call autoActivateManifestSpells(manifest, sessionId).
- maestro-cli/src/services/spell-auto-activator.ts reads `manifest.spells` and POSTs /api/spells/:id/activate per entry. Its docstring even says spells are "typically resolved from Task.spellIds at spawn time" — i.e., it expects a producer to populate them. If manifest.spells is empty/undefined it returns early (no-op).
- manifest-schema.ts:261 and types/manifest.ts accept `spells` with the description "Spells to auto-activate at session start (from Task.spellIds)".

PRODUCER SIDE IS MISSING:
- The on-disk manifest is produced solely by the CLI `manifest generate` command (server delegates: maestro-server/src/api/sessionRoutes.ts:138-151 invokes `maestro manifest generate --task-ids ... --skills ...` with NO spell args).
- ManifestGenerator.generateManifest (maestro-cli/src/commands/manifest-generator.ts:874) constructs the manifest object with manifestVersion/mode/tasks/session/context only — it NEVER sets `spells`.
- Its task mapping (lines 860-872) copies id/title/description/etc. but drops spellIds. TaskInput (line 24) doesn't even declare a spellIds field, and fetchTask (line 380) returns TaskInput, so spellIds is discarded at fetch time.
- Confirmed by exhaustive grep: NO `.spells =` assignment and NO `spells:` object-literal population anywhere in maestro-cli/src or maestro-server/src outside HookDispatcherService (an unrelated hook-outcome payload). `spellIds` appears only in: two doc-comments, server types.ts, and validation.ts (Zod acceptance) — never read to resolve into a manifest.

NET EFFECT: Assigning spells to a task (Task.spellIds) has zero effect at spawn. The manifest reaches the worker with no `spells`, autoActivateManifestSpells short-circuits, and task-attached spells never auto-activate. The whole P5 producer half is dead.

NOT THE DEFERRED ITEM: The brief's deferred note covers only "Task.spellIds Zod acceptance" — which IS implemented (validation.ts:151,174). But DESIGN_BRIEF.md explicitly scopes this in: line 20 "Task.spellIds, baked into manifest at spawn, auto-activate"; line 33 P5 "Task assignment (Task.spellIds, manifest, auto-activate)"; line 41 P2 "manifest.spells, spawn auto-activate". The manifest-population step is required and unimplemented — a real high-severity gap, not the verify-only deferred item.
verdict.fix:
Populate manifest.spells from Task.spellIds at the sole producer (the CLI manifest generator), since the server delegates manifest generation to it and passes no spell args.

1) maestro-cli/src/commands/manifest-generator.ts — TaskInput interface (line 24): add `spellIds?: string[];` so fetched task data retains it.

2) fetchTask (line 380): ensure the parsed task maps the server's spellIds into the returned TaskInput (e.g. `spellIds: raw.spellIds`).

3) In the generate handler around line 459-491: after fetching tasks, collect the unique set of spell IDs across all tasks, resolve each to {id, name} via the spells API (GET /api/spells/:id, or batch), and pass them into generateManifest. Then in generateManifest (line 874) add:
   `...(resolvedSpells && resolvedSpells.length > 0 && { spells: resolvedSpells }),`
   where resolvedSpells is ManifestSpell[] ({ id, name }).

   Minimal version if a name lookup is undesirable: carry just the IDs and let spell-auto-activator activate by id (it only strictly needs spell.id for the POST; spell.name is used for debug logging only). In that case skip the lookup and build `spells: uniqueSpellIds.map(id => ({ id, name: id }))`, or relax ManifestSpell.name to optional.

This restores the documented "Task.spellIds → baked into manifest at spawn → auto-activate" chain. The consumer (autoActivateManifestSpells) and schema already accept it, so no consumer changes are required. Add/extend a manifest-generator test asserting that tasks with spellIds yield a manifest.spells array.

confirmed.title: 'Pause' on an active spell silently deactivates it and loses iteration/cast-order state on resume
confirmed.detail: The ActiveSpellChip/Row menu exposes a Pause/Resume toggle bound to setSpellEnabled (ActiveSpellChip.tsx:65). setSpellEnabled(enabled=false) calls deactivateSpell, which on the server REMOVES the ActiveSpell from Session.activeSpells entirely (SpellService.deactivateSpell filters it out) and emits spell:deactivated, so the ring disappears. setSpellEnabled(enabled=true) calls activateSpell, which re-adds a fresh ActiveSpell with castAt=now and iteration=0. So 'Pause' is really 'Deactivate', and 'Resume' resets a continue-loop's iteration counter and re-orders the concentric rings (oldest-outermost ordering is by castAt). The ActiveSpell.enabled flag and matchActiveSpells' `if (!a.enabled) return false` gate were designed for a true pause that preserves state, but there is no endpoint to flip enabled without removal. The code comment admits the toggle endpoint is 'P2/P3', but the menu is live and mislabeled, producing user-visible wrong behavior (lost loop progress, jumped ring order).

verdict.title: 'Pause' on an active spell deactivates it and resets iteration/cast-order state on resume
verdict.reasoning:
Every claim in the finding is verifiable in the diff (git diff 3733ca6...HEAD):

1. ActiveSpellChipMenu.tsx:49-51 renders a live "Pause"/"Resume" menu item wired to onToggle. ActiveSpellChip.tsx:64-65 binds onToggle to setSpellEnabled(sessionId, active.spellId, !active.enabled). The menu is rendered (no feature gate) and the toggle is reachable from both the kebab and right-click.

2. useSpellActivationStore.ts:71-79 — setSpellEnabled is NOT a true enable/disable. For enabled=false it calls maestroClient.deactivateSpell; for enabled=true it calls maestroClient.activateSpell. The in-file comment explicitly admits the real toggle endpoint is 'P2/P3' and this is an optimistic deactivate/re-cast stand-in.

3. Server deactivateSpell (SpellService.ts:942) does `(session.activeSpells ?? []).filter(a => a.spellId !== spellId)` — it REMOVES the ActiveSpell entirely and emits spell:deactivated (line 947), so the ring/chip disappears rather than being marked paused.

4. Server activateSpell (SpellService.ts:903-916) re-adds a fresh ActiveSpell with iteration: 0 and castAt: now. So a 'Resume' wipes the continue-loop iteration counter (shown in the chip via active.iteration/maxIterations, ActiveSpellChip.tsx:31-33) back to 0.

5. The enabled flag and the dispatcher gate were designed for a real pause that preserves state: HookDispatcherService.ts:133 `if (!a.enabled) return false`, and ActiveSpell carries an `enabled` field. Nothing ever sets enabled to false via this path — it deletes instead — so the designed-for pause semantics are unused.

6. There is no endpoint to flip `enabled` without removal: spellRoutes.ts exposes only POST /spells/:id/activate and POST /spells/:id/deactivate (lines 196, 211). No PATCH/enabled toggle exists.

7. Ring ordering is by castAt: useActiveSpellsStore.ts:61-64 sortByCastAt is oldest-first → outermost. Because re-casting on resume sets castAt=now, the resumed spell jumps from its original ring position to the innermost ring — the user-visible 'jumped ring order'.

Net user-visible bugs: (a) Pause makes the spell's chip/ring vanish entirely instead of showing the paused state (the sp-chip--paused class and ⏸ glyph at ActiveSpellChip.tsx:37,54 are therefore dead code on this path); (b) Resume resets continue-loop iteration progress to 0; (c) Resume reorders the concentric rings. The label says 'Pause' but the behavior is 'Deactivate'.

This is genuinely user-visible and not on the known-deferred list (the deferred list covers /api/skills, resetIteration endpoint, ensemble-create stub, and Task.spellIds Zod — not the pause-toggle mislabeling). Severity medium is fair: no data corruption, but lost loop progress and confusing UX.
verdict.fix:
Minimal, low-risk fix until the real enabled-toggle endpoint lands: stop pretending this is a pause. Remove/disable the Pause/Resume menu item so the chip only offers Deactivate (which is what the code actually does), avoiding the mislabel and the silent state loss.

In maestro-ui/src/components/spells/ActiveSpellChipMenu.tsx, drop the toggle button (lines 49-51) — and remove the now-unused `enabled`/`onToggle` props — leaving Reset loop / Deactivate / View in Spellbook / Edit trigger. Correspondingly drop the onToggle wiring in ActiveSpellChip.tsx:64-65.

Alternatively (slightly larger, preferred if the team wants pause now): add a real toggle that preserves state instead of remove+recast:
  - Server: add SpellService.setSpellEnabled(spellId, sessionIds, enabled) that maps over session.activeSpells and sets a.enabled without dropping the entry or touching iteration/castAt, emitting a spell:updated event. Expose it as POST /spells/:id/enabled (body { targetSessionIds[], enabled }) in spellRoutes.ts.
  - UI: point useSpellActivationStore.setSpellEnabled at the new endpoint (replacing the deactivate/activate branch at lines 74-78) and have useActiveSpellsStore patch the existing row's `enabled` in place rather than re-running activate (which resets castAt/iteration). verdict.title: continue-loop seeded on UserPromptSubmit (Plan-First) makes exit 2 block the user's first prompt instead of continuing
verdict.reasoning:
Verified end-to-end against the diff and ground-truth design.

CHAIN (all live in this diff):
1. SPELL_LIBRARY seed `spell_plan_first` (FileSystemSpellRepository.ts:60-74) has action:'continue-loop', loopType:'plan-execute', trigger.hookEvent:'UserPromptSubmit', maxIterations:2.
2. HookDispatcherService.execContinueLoop (lines 253-284) returns {continue:true, reason} and bumps iteration whenever the spell matches — it does NOT consider which hook event fired.
3. composeResult (lines 369-422) returns exitCode:2 for ANY continuing outcome (lines 390-407), event-agnostic. The inline comment even says 'exit 2 on Stop tells Claude to keep going' — but the code applies it to every event.
4. hooks.json (maestro-cli/plugins/maestro-worker/hooks/hooks.json:67-83) binds UserPromptSubmit -> `maestro hook dispatch UserPromptSubmit`, so the event is actually dispatched.
5. CLI applyResult (hook.ts:99-107) unconditionally writes result.reason to stderr and process.exit(2) when exitCode===2, regardless of event.

PROTOCOL CLAIM (load-bearing, confirmed by ground truth): Claude Code hook exit-2 semantics are event-specific. On Stop, exit 2 forces continuation. On UserPromptSubmit, exit 2 BLOCKS the submitted prompt and surfaces stderr to the user as an error. The DESIGN_BRIEF.md:18 explicitly maps the taxonomy as 'gate (PreToolUse exit 2 + reason) ... continue-loop (Stop exit 2, capped)'. The 4-actions-hook-protocol.excalidraw diagram states 'continue-loop: Stop exit 2 re-drive' and, for the plan-execute loop type specifically, 'plan -> gate execution' — neither is 'continue-loop on UserPromptSubmit'. So the seed contradicts the frozen design on two counts.

RESULT: Activating Plan-First makes the agent's very first UserPromptSubmit get blocked/erased with the loop-continuation text 'Loop "Plan-First" iteration 1/2: now execute the plan you wrote...' shown as an error — the opposite of plan-then-execute. The reason text itself ('now execute the plan you wrote') presumes a plan already exists, which only makes sense on a Stop re-drive, further confirming the intended binding is Stop.

The sibling seed spell_self_critic (continue-loop on Stop, lines 45-59) is the correct precedent. No tests pin UserPromptSubmit for this spell (grep of maestro-server/test, maestro-cli/test found none), so the seed change is safe. Not in the known-deferred list. isReal:true.
verdict.fix:
Primary (minimal): In maestro-server/src/infrastructure/repositories/FileSystemSpellRepository.ts, change spell_plan_first's trigger from UserPromptSubmit to Stop, matching the action taxonomy (continue-loop = Stop exit 2) and the spell_self_critic precedent:

(line 68; was hookEvent: 'UserPromptSubmit'). The existing loop reason text 'now execute the plan you wrote' already assumes prior planning, so a Stop-bound re-drive reads correctly.

confirmed.title: Hook dispatch trusts body sessionId with no caller-ownership check (cross-session control)
confirmed.file: maestro-server/src/api/hookRoutes.ts:16-20 + HookDispatcherService.ts:49-54; CLI sends X-Session-Id at hook.ts:74 but server ignores it
confirmed.detail: POST /api/hooks/dispatch reads sessionId from the request BODY (hookDispatchSchema) and acts on session.activeSpells for that id, with no verification that the authenticated caller is that session or its coordinator. The CLI dutifully sends an X-Session-Id header (hook.ts:74) but the server never reads it. Any authenticated client/agent can therefore dispatch arbitrary hook events for ANY other session: force a continue-loop (re-drive another agent's Stop, persisting an iteration bump via sessionRepo.update in execContinueLoop), inject prompts into another session's PTY (execInjectPrompt emits session:prompt_send), or trigger notify-channel side effects. Existing cross-session operations in this codebase DO gate the caller (sessionRoutes.ts:1382-1413 requires X-Session-Id and coordinator role to spawn), so this is an inconsistency, not a deliberate trust model. Recommendation: require X-Session-Id to equal body.sessionId (or be its coordinator) before dispatching.

verdict.title: Hook dispatch trusts body sessionId with no caller-ownership check (cross-session control)
verdict.reasoning:

Also note /sessions/:id/prompt trusts a body senderSessionId for attribution (1198) so the model isn't perfectly uniform — but it still blocks self-prompt and can't drive the iteration/loop machinery, and the strongest precedents (spawn, mode) gate via header. confirmed.title: User-controlled spell matcher compiled to RegExp on the hot hook path (ReDoS / event-loop stall)
confirmed.file: maestro-server/src/application/services/HookDispatcherService.ts:158-166; matcher validated only as z.string().max(500) in validation.ts spellTriggerSchema
confirmed.detail: matcherMatches() does `new RegExp(matcher).test(target)` synchronously, where matcher comes from spell create/update (createSpellSchema/updateSpellSchema -> spellTriggerSchema, validated only as a <=500-char string, no regex-safety). This runs on EVERY hook dispatch (PreToolUse/PostToolUse fire constantly) against attacker-influenceable targets (tool_name, file_path, message, or the full JSON.stringify(payload) fallback at matcherTarget:148-155). A catastrophic-backtracking pattern (e.g. '(a+)+$') against a crafted target blocks the single-threaded Node event loop for the whole server, stalling all sessions. The matcher is operator-set, so this is mainly a robustness/DoS-via-footgun issue rather than unauthenticated RCE, but there is no regex timeout, no safe-regex linting, and no try/catch around test() for runaway evaluation (the catch only handles invalid-syntax compile errors). Recommendation: run matcher matching with a timeout (e.g. RE2/safe-regex) or cap target length and reject pathological patterns at create time.

verdict.title: User-controlled spell matcher compiled to RegExp on the hot hook path (ReDoS / event-loop stall)
verdict.reasoning: Verified against the diff (git diff 3733ca6...HEAD). HookDispatcherService.ts is entirely new (434 insertions) and contains matcherMatches() at lines 158-166 which does `new RegExp(matcher).test(target)` synchronously. The matcher originates from spellTriggerSchema in validation.ts:529, validated only as `z.string().max(500).optional()` with no regex-safety check. This code is on the real dispatch path: hookRoutes.ts:16-18 (POST /api/hooks/dispatch) -> dispatcher.dispatch() -> matchActiveSpells() (line 56) -> filter callback (lines 132-138) -> matcherMatches(). The filter only invokes the regex for spells that are enabled, match the event, and carry a non-empty matcher (lines 133-135), so the cost is gated by the presence of an active matcher-bearing spell — but PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks fire constantly, so any single pathological matcher stalls the whole single-threaded Node event loop, freezing all sessions. The target is attacker-influenceable and length-uncapped: matcherTarget() (lines 141-156) uses tool_name, or for generic events path/file_path/message/JSON.stringify(payload). The try/catch at 160-165 only catches invalid-regex compile errors and falls back to substring includes — it provides zero protection against catastrophic backtracking inside test(), which throws nothing and just hangs. There is no regex timeout, no safe-regex/RE2, and no target length cap. The finding's own medium severity and footgun-DoS (not RCE, since matchers are operator-set) framing is accurate. Confirmed not pre-existing — the whole file is new in this redesign, so it is in scope.
verdict.fix: Defense in depth at two points. (1) Reject pathological/invalid patterns at create/update time: in validation.ts replace `matcher: z.string().max(500).optional()` in spellTriggerSchema with a refinement that (a) compiles the pattern to confirm valid syntax and (b) runs it through a safe-regex check, e.g. `matcher: z.string().max(500).refine(m => { try { new RegExp(m); } catch { return false; } return safeRegex(m); }, { message: 'matcher must be a valid, non-backtracking regular expression' }).optional()` (add the `safe-regex` dependency, which is tiny and synchronous). (2) Make the runtime path resilient regardless of stored data, since legacy/imported spells bypass new validation: in HookDispatcherService.matcherMatches() cap the evaluated target length and avoid unbounded regex on huge inputs — `private matcherMatches(matcher: string, target: string): boolean { if (!target) return false; const t = target.length > 4096 ? target.slice(0, 4096) : target; try { const re = new RegExp(matcher); return re.test(t); } catch { return t.includes(matcher); } }`. For full protection against backtracking on already-stored unsafe patterns, prefer compiling with a linear-time engine (RE2 via the `re2` package: `const re = new RE2(matcher)`), which eliminates catastrophic backtracking entirely and keeps the existing test() call shape; the length cap alone is a cheaper interim mitigation. Validation-time rejection (1) is the minimal, dependency-light fix that closes the create/update vector; (2) hardens the hot path for pre-existing/legacy data.

confirmed.title: Seed (isDefault) spells can be mutated via PUT, silently weakening gate/fail-closed library spells
confirmed.detail: DELETE is correctly guarded for seed spells (SEED_IDS / isDefault, repo lines 283-296). confirmed.title: Ensemble outermost ring never uses the ensemble color — ensembleColorId is dropped at every ring host

(3) CLI applyResult (hook.ts L92-97) writes result.stdout to process.stdout UNCONDITIONALLY for every action — and its own comment (L93) says it forwards stdout for "feed-context / inject-prompt," directly contradicting the server comment at L220-221 which falsely claims the CLI only forwards stdout for feed-context. The CLI comment is the accurate one; the server comment is the false rationalization the finding flagged. (4) Nothing in the Spell/ActiveSpell types, validation.ts, or the matcher couples action to hookEvent, so an inject-prompt spell may legally carry trigger.hookEvent UserPromptSubmit or SessionStart. The frozen action taxonomy in docs/spell-system-design/4-actions-hook-protocol.excalidraw maps inject-prompt -> PTY and feed-context -> hook stdout (events: UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart), so inject-prompt is supposed to be PTY-only; returning stdout re-introduces the double-inject bug class P1 was meant to kill.

Two corrections to the finding's framing: (a) Reachability is narrower than stated. NO seeded spell triggers it — the only default inject-prompt spell is spell_progress_pulse bound to Notification (FileSystemSpellRepository.ts L75-88), and Claude does not fold hook stdout into context on Notification (only UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart do). The seeded UserPromptSubmit and SessionStart spells are continue-loop and feed-context. So the bug fires only for a USER-CREATED inject-prompt spell bound to UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart — a real latent hazard but not an out-of-the-box one. (b) The implementation is actually consistent with the P2 protocol contract as documented in types.ts L757/L796 ("exit 0 + stdout for inject-prompt / feed-context"), so the stdout is deliberate, not an accidental leak — but that documented contract itself contradicts the frozen taxonomy diagram. Either way the concrete double-delivery on context-surfacing hooks is real. Verdict: real, medium severity, latent (custom-spell-reachable).

verdict.title: spell:activated WS payload omits the spell name, so ring tooltips/selectors show raw IDs
verdict.reasoning:
Verified end-to-end against the diff and dependent files.

1. Server emit (SpellService.ts activateSpell, in the diff): emits `spell:activated` with `{ spellId, sessionIds, activeSpell: sessions[0].activeSpell, timestamp }`. The payload carries no `name`/`spellName`.

2. The `activeSpell` object is an `ActiveSpell` (types.ts:667-678): fields are spellId, color, enabled, hookEvent, matcher, iteration, ensembleId, castAt, castBy — NO name. Confirmed.

3. UI handler (useMaestroStore.ts:572): `spellName: activeSpell.spellName ?? message.data.spellName ?? spellId`. Neither `activeSpell.spellName` nor `message.data.spellName` exists on the payload, so it falls back to the raw `spellId`. Confirmed verbatim.

4. The store (useActiveSpellsStore.ts:69-80) stores `spellName` as-is with no friendly-name resolution.

5. All three ring hosts (SessionListItem.tsx:238, AppWorkspace.tsx:55, SpacesRail.tsx:66) build `RingSpec.spellName` from that stored value, and spellRings.ts:76-82 emits it into `data-spell-ring-names` (CSV).

6. UI_SPEC §7 (UI_SPEC.md:41) + uispec/02-ux-flows.md:214 declare `data-spell-ring-names` the canonical source for the ring tooltip AND e2e selectors (ux-flows depends on it), with the example value "Guardian,Test Sentinel,+2".

7. Decisive: FileSystemSpellRepository.ts SPELL_LIBRARY seeds `id:'spell_guardian', name:'Guardian'`, etc. So the tooltip/selector literally shows `spell_guardian` instead of `Guardian` — exactly the finding's example. For user-created spells the id is `spell_<timestamp>` (TimestampIdGenerator), which is worse (opaque).

This breaks the frozen ring-name contract and the e2e selectors that depend on it. The same defect also affects the reconnect/refetch path (hydrateActiveSpellsFromSession reads `s.spellName` at L89, and the persisted ActiveSpell has no name → fallback at store L101), but the reported activation path alone is sufficient to confirm the bug. Not in the known-deferred list.

verdict.title: run-command seed spells (Test Sentinel, Lint-on-Edit) are silent no-ops
verdict.reasoning:
Verified against the P2 dispatcher commit (16dcac9; the cited file maestro-server/src/application/services/HookDispatcherService.ts does not exist on the literal checked-out HEAD 568611c, which is P1-only, but exists verbatim in the parallel P2 commit — same code, different hash).

Every specific claim is confirmed:
- execRunCommand begins at line 286 and reads `(spell as any).command` / `(spell as any).commandArgs`.
- The Spell interface in types.ts has NO command/commandArgs field (full field list: id, name, description, icon, color, action, loopType, trigger, failMode, maxIterations, skillRef, isDefault, createdAt, updatedAt). So the `as any` cast always yields undefined.
- With cmd falsy, execRunCommand returns `{ spellId, action:'run-command', stdout:'' }` — a genuine no-op (it never reaches the execFile branch).
- The dispatch switch in executeAction (L186-187) routes `case 'run-command'` to execRunCommand, so the path is reachable, not dead code.
- Seed spells spell_test_sentinel and spell_lint_on_edit (FileSystemSpellRepository.ts L31-44 and L107-120) both set action:'run-command', isDefault:true, trigger.enabled:true, and set no command — so activating either reaches execRunCommand and does nothing.

This is NOT a duplicate of any known-deferred item (the allowlist covers /api/skills P6, resetIteration P3, ensemble-create UI P4, Task.spellIds Zod P5 — run-command/HookExecutor is not listed). The brief (DESIGN_BRIEF.md L18) maps run-command to 'HookExecutor' and the code comment states real shell execution arrives with the CLI HookExecutor in a follow-up, so it is a documented v1 limitation — correctly rated severity:low (graceful no-op, failMode:open, intentional guard against arbitrary code execution from spell content). The user-facing concern stands: 2 of 9 curated spells appear functional in the library/UI but are inert when activated.
verdict.fix:
Minimal fix is honesty-surfacing rather than implementing shell exec (which is intentionally deferred to the CLI HookExecutor). Two low-effort options, pick one:

1. (Preferred, smallest) Mark the two run-command seed spells as not-yet-wired so the UI/library doesn't present them as working. Add a flag to the Spell entity (e.g. `comingSoon?: boolean`) and set it on spell_test_sentinel and spell_lint_on_edit in FileSystemSpellRepository.ts, then disable/badge them in the curated library so users can't activate an inert spell. This avoids the "looks like it works but silently does nothing" trap.

2. (Alternative) Make the no-op observable instead of silent: in execRunCommand, when cmd is missing, return a reason/error rather than empty stdout, e.g.
   return { spellId: spell.id, action: 'run-command', reason: `${spell.name}: run-command not yet wired (HookExecutor pending)` };
so the dispatcher surfaces the deferral through the existing reason channel (stderr) instead of an empty pass-through that reads as success.

Either keeps the deliberate "don't shell out implicitly" safety stance while removing the false impression that Test Sentinel / Lint-on-Edit are functional.
